Project.Name: content-delivery.xml
Project.Title: Content Delivery Modernization: Distribution Point Consolidation

Task.Name: Phase 0 — Analysis of the existing estate
C0.1 Validated endpoint count: Configuration Manager clients reconciled with Intune and the asset record, duplicates and stale records removed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-0-3

Task.Name: C0.2 Distribution point inventory: every DP with its site, office, OS version, hardware age and warranty, PXE and Connected Cache roles, and content library size
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-0-3

Task.Name: C0.3 Circuit data per office: bandwidth, peak use, monthly cost and renewal date, from telecom contract records
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-0-1

Task.Name: C0.4 Packaging inventory: every application and package, its installer type, install count, active deployments and last change
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Packaging team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-0-3

Task.Name: C0.5 Funding ask decomposed: acquisition or five-year total cost of ownership, and every item beyond the distribution point itemized
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Budget officer Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-2

Task.Name: C0.7 Content library measured on one DP; sizing run against 4,000 clients per DP with a draft hub design and office wave order
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-1-2

Task.Name: D-C1 Target distribution point count when co-management completes, and the fiscal year
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO Options: A dated target count from the validated endpoint count and Microsoft's 4,000-clients-per-DP limit (about 24 in the worked case); keep the current count (then say why the office count, not the client count, sizes it) If decided late: No refresh or consolidation can be sized, and the decision on the funding ask waits Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-1-2

Task.Name: C0.6 Assessment worksheet completed from agency data, reviewed by the endpoint lead, ISSO and budget officer, and kept inside the boundary
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Content delivery project lead Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-2

Task.Name: CG0 Gate 0 — Inventory and decomposition complete
Task.Contact: Content delivery project lead and ISSO
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Content delivery project lead and ISSO Criteria: Endpoint count validated and dated; every distribution point in the inventory and the system component inventory; circuit cost and renewal date recorded per office; packaging inventory complete; the ask stated as acquisition or five-year cost with scope itemized; a dated target DP count; the worksheet reviewed and stored inside the boundary Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-0-4

Task.Name: Phase 1 — Decision on the funding ask, and Stage 1 in a test hierarchy
D-C2 Decision on the funding ask
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO Options: Refresh in place; consolidate to a hub tier (the guide's recommendation where the circuits allow); cloud-first with Connected Cache, keeping a hub tier only until the five gates close If decided late: Refresh money is committed by default, or the hub build can't start Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-2

Task.Name: C1.1 Budget submission revised to the chosen option, the worked case's planning assumptions replaced by Phase 0 data, and its consistency with Intune-first stated
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Budget officer Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-2

Task.Name: CG1 Gate 1 — Funding decision recorded
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO Criteria: Option chosen with the decision table and worksheet as its evidence; budget submission revised; target DP count and fiscal year recorded; the decision filed in the program's decision register Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-2

Task.Name: C1.2 Stage 1: Lab 2 run end to end in a test hierarchy, every change applied and then backed out from its plan.csv
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#lab-2

Task.Name: D-C10 Stage 1 to Stage 2: go/no-go for production
Task.Contact: Content delivery project lead and ISSO
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Content delivery project lead and ISSO Options: Go when Lab 2 ran end to end with its back-out, every cmdlet ran on the agency's Configuration Manager version, the inventory matched the console and the change board approved the production plan; no-go repeats Stage 1 If decided late: No production change can start, and the hub build waits Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#go-no-go

Task.Name: Phase 2 — Hub content tier
D-C3 Hub sites and distribution points per hub
Task.Contact: Endpoint lead and network engineering lead
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead and network engineering lead Options: Existing regional facilities inside the current boundary, two pull DPs each, with source DPs at the two data centers (the worked case: 12 sites, 24 DPs); more hubs where latency or headcount needs them If decided late: Hub servers can't be ordered or built Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-1-1

Task.Name: C2.1 Hub DP servers built on Windows Server 2019 or later: IIS, BITS and Remote Differential Compression; CM-6 baseline applied and scanned; HTTPS with a PKI certificate; added to the inventory and the SSP
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-3-1

Task.Name: C2.2 Pull DPs added at each hub, sourcing from the data center DPs; one distribution point group per hub (New-DpcHubTier.ps1 -Apply)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-3-2

Task.Name: C2.3 Content distributed to each hub group; distribution status clean; content validation run; inventory rerun
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-3-3

Task.Name: CG2 Gate 2 — Hub tier serving content
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager lead and ISSO Criteria: Every hub DP in production, baselined, scanned and in the SSP; every package distributed to its region's group with no failures; load per DP under 3,200 clients (80% of the published 4,000); change records for every server Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-3-3

Task.Name: Phase 3 — Peer caching and boundary groups
C3.1 Boundary groups for the pilot wave: hub DPs added, peer options set, the other hubs as timed fallback, never to the default site group (Set-DpcBoundaryGroups.ps1 -Apply)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-4-2

Task.Name: D-C4 Client-to-client traffic on branch segments: TCP 8003, UDP 8004 and TCP 7680
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: Allow within each office's subnet only; allow for named peer cache sources only; block, and size circuits for hub pulls If decided late: Peer cache and Delivery Optimization peering can't be configured, and the pilot measures nothing Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-5

Task.Name: X-E14 Co-management on for the pilot collection (Endpoint plan E1.4)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint & Device project If decided late: Pilot devices have no Intune channel for Delivery Optimization policy Source: endpoint-device.md

Task.Name: C3.2 Peer cache sources chosen per pilot office (desktop chassis, disk, always on); client settings deployed; partial download on; BranchCache enabled
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-5-2

Task.Name: C3.3 Delivery Optimization through Intune: Group download mode with a group ID per office, or subnet restriction, for the pilot devices
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-5-3

Task.Name: C3.4 Pilot measurement at the pilot offices: bytes from peers, from the hub and from the office DP, for a month of deployments
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-5-4

Task.Name: CG3 Gate 3 — Pilot offices served from hubs and peers
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Criteria: Pilot offices' content served by the hub and peers, with the office DP in read-only fallback and serving under a threshold the endpoint lead sets; no deployment failure traced to content location; measurement report filed Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#go-no-go

Task.Name: Phase 4 — Office waves
X-NG3 Pilot sites governed and evidenced on new transport (Network plan Gate 3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network & Access project If decided late: The pilot offices are still on their old circuits, and the first wave of DP retirements waits Source: network-access.md

Task.Name: C4.1 Pilot wave: each office DP checked, drained, watched 30 days, removed with its site system; disks sanitized; inventory and SSP updated
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-6

Task.Name: D-C5 Wave plan: offices ordered by circuit readiness and renewal date
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Content delivery project lead Options: By circuit readiness and renewal (the guide's order); by region (simpler, but waits on the slowest circuit in each) If decided late: Wave 2 can't be scheduled, and offices keep DPs they no longer need Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-1-2

Task.Name: C4.2 Wave 2, about 25% of offices: boundary groups moved, peers enabled, office DPs read-only, then retired after 30 clean days
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-6

Task.Name: C4.3 Wave 3, about 60% of offices cumulative
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-6

Task.Name: C4.4 Wave 4, every remaining office, or a dated exception with its reason
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-6

Task.Name: CG4 Gate 4 — No branch distribution point left
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO Criteria: Every office DP retired or in the exception register with a date and reason; every retired server's media sanitized and its inventory and SSP entries closed; hub load per DP still under 80% of the published limit Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-6-5

Task.Name: Phase 5 — Packaging on one standard
D-C6 Packaging standard
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Options: PSAppDeployToolkit as the standard wrapper, version pinned, for every app that isn't a clean MSI; vendor installers with Intune's PowerShell script installer only; a mix by app class If decided late: Repackaging can't start, and the client apps workload waits Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-7

Task.Name: C5.1 Standard template: pinned toolkit version, signed scripts, one log path, exit codes mapped, detection rule pattern; held under change control
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Packaging team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-7-2

Task.Name: C5.2 Catalog rationalized: apps nobody installs retired, duplicate versions removed, an owner for every app kept
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Packaging team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-7-1

Task.Name: C5.3 Most-installed apps repackaged on the template; each tested from Configuration Manager and as an .intunewin from Intune
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Packaging team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-7-5

Task.Name: C5.4 Rest of the catalog repackaged or retired
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Packaging team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-7-5

Task.Name: CG5 Gate 5 — Catalog on the standard wrapper
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Criteria: Every kept app has an owner, a package on the template, a tested detection rule and a change record; the same package installs from either tool; retired apps removed from both Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-7-1

Task.Name: Phase 6 — Content workloads to Intune
C6.1 Client apps and Office Click-to-Run apps workloads: Pilot Intune, then Intune; apps published as Win32 apps from the standard packages
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-8-1

Task.Name: C6.2 Configuration Manager required and available deployments withdrawn as each app moves; the count reported weekly
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-8-2

Task.Name: X-EG3 Workloads cut over, including Windows Update policies and device configuration (Endpoint plan Gate 3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint & Device project If decided late: Update content still comes from Configuration Manager, and retirement gate 2 can't close Source: endpoint-device.md

Task.Name: C6.3 Configuration Manager software-update client setting turned off for every device on the Windows Update workload
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-8-3

Task.Name: X-E15 Intune-first intake with Autopilot registration (Endpoint plan E1.5)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint & Device project If decided late: There's no Autopilot path to move bare-metal provisioning onto Source: endpoint-device.md

Task.Name: D-C7 OS provisioning for existing devices
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Options: Windows Autopilot for every rebuild, with reset where it applies; keep task sequences for a named exception class on a hub DP until it can move If decided late: Imaging keeps a PXE distribution point alive, and retirement gate 3 stays open Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-8-4

Task.Name: C6.4 Bare-metal provisioning moved from task sequences to Autopilot; PXE turned off on every DP
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-8-4

Task.Name: C6.5 Compliance and Endpoint Protection evidence sourced from Intune and Defender, not the Configuration Manager site database; ISSO confirms
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-8-5

Task.Name: Phase 7 — Connected Cache at the hubs
D-C8 Connected Cache form and placement
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead and ISSO Options: Connected Cache for Enterprise and Education on its own host at each hub, its Azure resource placed in the boundary analysis; the Configuration Manager-integrated cache on a hub DP with no other roles (then retirement gate 4 binds it); none, where measured circuits carry cloud content If decided late: Cloud content keeps crossing every hub circuit, and gate 4 has no plan Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-9

Task.Name: C7.1 Cache hosts built at the hubs on a supported OS, nothing else on port 80; Delivery Optimization pointed at each office's hub cache
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-9-1

Task.Name: C7.2 Cache hit rate measured; Win32 app, update and Microsoft 365 Apps content confirmed served from the hubs
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint engineering Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-9-2

Task.Name: C7.3 Connected Cache turned off on any DP hardware once the hub cache serves that office
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-9-3

Task.Name: Phase 8 — The five retirement gates
RG1 Retirement gate 1 — App content
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Criteria: Client apps and Office Click-to-Run workloads on Intune for the whole validated population, and no required or available deployment still published from Configuration Manager Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-1

Task.Name: RG2 Retirement gate 2 — Update content
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Criteria: Windows Update policies and device configuration workloads on Intune, and Configuration Manager's software-update client setting off for those devices Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-1

Task.Name: RG3 Retirement gate 3 — OS provisioning
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead Criteria: Bare-metal provisioning on Autopilot; no task sequence or PXE service still in use Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-1

Task.Name: RG4 Retirement gate 4 — Caching role
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead and ISSO Criteria: No Connected Cache instance runs on distribution-point hardware, or none is needed on the measured circuits Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-1

Task.Name: RG5 Retirement gate 5 — Compliance evidence
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Criteria: Compliance and Endpoint Protection reporting no longer cite the Configuration Manager site database as their evidence source Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-1

Task.Name: D-C9 Retire the hub distribution point tier
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO Options: Retire it in the week the last gate closes; keep it while any gate is open. Never on a date alone If decided late: Twenty-odd servers stay in the boundary to be patched, scanned and accredited for no workload Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-1

Task.Name: C8.1 Hub and source DPs drained and removed with their site systems (Invoke-DpcOfficeRetirement.ps1 -GatesPath); media sanitized; inventory and SSP entries closed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-2

Task.Name: C8.2 Cleanup: distribution point groups removed, boundary group site-system references cleared, peer cache client settings and deployments retired; no DP role left in the hierarchy
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Configuration Manager team Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-3

Task.Name: CG8 Gate 8 — Last distribution point retired, site roles cleaned up, evidence complete
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO and ISSO Criteria: All five retirement gates closed in a gates run; no distribution point role left in Get-CMSiteRole; every DP's decommission record, sanitization record and SSP change filed; the content delivery evidence set in the guide's requirements table complete Source: ../books/guides/dp-consolidation-implementation.md#step-10-3

Task.Name: X-G3 Program G3 — Rollout Complete
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and steering committee Source: program-master-schedule.md
